newsitem.title: CHINA: China cotton demand seen at 5 mln tonnes in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China cotton demand seen at 5 mln tonnes in 1997.

text.p: China's demand for cotton was seen at 5.0 million tonnes in 1997, the Economic Information Daily said on Friday.
A drop in China's cotton output last year coupled with quality problems of the domestic product meant imports this year would be at a "relatively high level", the newspaper said.
But the poor harvest in 1996 had pushed international prices up, making imports less attractive, it said.
China's textile sector would need 3.3 million tonnes of cotton while demand from other industries and for reserves would be 1.7 million tonnes, it said.
The latest official figures showed cotton imports reached 590,000 tonnes in the first 11 months of 1996, down 14.4 percent from the same period a year ago.
The government would not change the purchase price of cotton in 1997, it said, but gave no further details.
China's cotton output in 1996 was estimated at 4.0 million tonnes, down by 800,000 tonnes from the year before, according to the latest official figures.
